name: Khongjom War Memorial Complex
description: Memorial complex on Kheba Ching hill in Khongjom, Thoubal district, commemorating the decisive Battle of Khongjom (23 April 1891) during the Anglo-Manipur War. Features a tall sword monument, gardens, and tributes to Manipuri warriors including Major Paona Brajabasi who resisted British forces.
facts: Site of the last major battle of the Anglo-Manipur War of 1891
About 32-36 km southeast of Imphal on NH-102
Hosts annual Khongjom Day observances on 23 April
Includes world's tallest sword statue according to local sources
Tourist home functioning since 1988

name: Senapati Town
description: District headquarters of Senapati (also known as Tahamzam), a hill town on NH-2 about 62 km north of Imphal, serving as gateway to northern Manipur hills with mixed ethnic communities including Mao, Maram and Poumai Nagas.
facts: Named after Tikendrajit Singh (Senapati); local name Tahamzam means 'Hill of Butterflies'
Elevation around 1500 m
On National Highway 2 linking Imphal to Nagaland

name: Willong Khullen Megaliths
description: Prehistoric megalithic site in Willong Khullen village, Mao-Maram area of Senapati district, featuring over 100-130 standing stones up to 7 m high, often compared to Stonehenge. Erected by ancient Maram Naga clans for warrior feats and feasts of merit.
facts: About 37 km from Maram on Maram-Peren Road
One of the largest megalithic complexes in Northeast India
Village is traditional Maram Naga settlement

name: Makhel Village
description: Sacred ancestral village in Senapati district believed to be the dispersal point of Naga tribes. Features sacred banyan trees (said to grow from Naga mother's tomb), farewell monolith, triomonolith, hailstorm stone and other historical monuments.
facts: Near Tadubi; sacred for multiple ethnic communities
Dispersal Tree at nearby Sajouba
Important for anthropologists studying Naga migration

name: Mao Gate
description: Historic border town and gateway on the Manipur-Nagaland boundary in Senapati district at about 1788 m elevation. Oldest hill station in the area, commercial stop on NH-2 with scenic hills and traditional Mao Naga culture.
facts: Northern entry point to Manipur from Nagaland
Base for treks to Dzuko Valley from Manipur side
Multi-ethnic commercial hub

name: Dzuko Valley (Manipur Side)
description: High-altitude valley (around 2450 m) straddling the Manipur-Nagaland border in Senapati and Kohima districts. Famous for rolling meadows, seasonal Dzuko lily (Lilium chitrangadae), wildflowers, and trekking. Manipur access from Mao/Mount Iso area.
facts: Shared with Nagaland; boundary disputed
Snow in winter, lily blooms in summer
Highest peak of Manipur Mount Iso (Tenipu) nearby

name: Maram Khullen
description: One of the largest and oldest traditional villages of the Maram Naga tribe in Senapati district. Preserves hereditary chieftainship, carved wooden houses, terraced fields and indigenous crafts; origin point of the Barak River.
facts: About 18 km from Senapati town
Attracts anthropologists
Traditional social structure intact

name: Purul Village
description: Traditional Poumai Naga village (also Hiimai Phii) in Senapati, known for indigenous games like Toutou and wrestling during festivals, stone steps and cultural heritage. Home to Poula language speakers.
facts: About 19-20 km from Maram on NH-2
Elevation around 1867 m
Consists of Purul Akutpa and Atongba

name: Yangkhullen Village
description: Historic hilltop village in Senapati district built on a steep incline, traditional Zeme or related Naga settlement with preserved lifestyle, natural beauty and cultural significance.
facts: Listed as places of interest on official district site
About 26-75 km depending on route from Senapati
Traditional architecture on steep terrain

name: Dziiduri Highland
description: Emerging eco-tourism highland at ~1960 m in Paomata block near Khumai (Tunggam) village, Senapati. Features wetland, Dziitrulai Waterfall, Abulya Cliff, sacred Natousalai site, views of Mount Iso, terraced fields and developing trekking infrastructure.
facts: Promoted as state eco-tourism gem
Views of Manipur's highest peak
Community-led development by KYSO and HEAT-M

name: Naamai Zho Eco Tourism Park
description: Scenic grassland and eco-tourism site near Koide village in Senapati, famous for cosmos flower blooms and annual Cosmos Flower Festival. Offers viewpoints and nature photography amid paddy fields and hills.
facts: Hosts Cosmos Flower Festival attracting thousands
About 5-6 km from Maram Bazar
Adopted home to colorful cosmos flowers

name: Loktak Lake
description: Largest freshwater lake in Northeast India in Bishnupur district, famous for floating phumdis (heterogeneous biomass islands). Ramsar wetland supporting unique ecosystem, traditional fishing, and the only floating national park.
facts: Surface area typically ~287 km², varies seasonally 250-500 km²
Ramsar site since 23 March 1990 (site no. 463)
Etymology from Meitei: Lok=stream, Tak=end
Home to floating islands used for fishing and agriculture

name: Keibul Lamjao National Park
description: World's only floating national park on the southeastern phumdis of Loktak Lake in Bishnupur district. Last natural habitat of the endangered Sangai (Manipur brow-antlered deer), Manipur's state animal.
facts: Area ~40 km²; established as sanctuary 1966, national park 1977
UNESCO tentative list as Keibul Lamjao Conservation Area
Phumdis support the deer; floating and sinking cycle disrupted by Ithai Barrage
Best visited early morning for Sangai sighting

name: INA Martyrs' Memorial Complex
description: Historic memorial and museum complex in Moirang, Bishnupur district, where the Indian National Army first hoisted the Indian tricolour on liberated Indian soil on 14 April 1944 under Col. Shaukat Ali Malik. Includes museum with INA artifacts.
facts: Site of INA headquarters for ~3 months in 1944
Memorial complex expanded and unveiled in 2005; cenotaph from 1969
About 45 km south of Imphal
Near Moirang Kangla where flag was raised

name: Bishnupur Vishnu Temple
description: 15th-century conical brick temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu in Bishnupur town, from which the district derives its name. Built by King Kyamba after receiving an idol from the Pong king following a military victory.
facts: Protected historical monument under ASI
Bishnupur means 'abode of Vishnu'
About 27 km from Imphal on Tiddim Road
Associated with Vaishnavite influence in Manipur

name: Red Hill (Maibam Lotpa Ching)
description: WWII battlefield hillock in Nambol area of Bishnupur district, about 17 km south of Imphal on Tiddim Road. Site of fierce fighting between Allied and Japanese forces; features India Peace Memorial and Japanese cemetery.
facts: Japanese war veterans constructed the India Peace Memorial
Imphal Peace Museum nearby with war relics
Pilgrimage site for Japanese and British visitors
Also known as Maibam Lotpa Ching

name: Phubala
description: Charming resort village on the western fringes of Loktak Lake in Bishnupur district, about 40 km south of Imphal. Popular for boating, lake views, and local culture; linked to Khamba-Thoibi folklore.
facts: On western bank of Loktak
Featured in Manipuri folklore (Phubala Hanuba)
Access for water sports and lake exploration

name: Loukoipat Ecological Park
description: Eco-park with a small lake surrounded by green hillocks near Bishnupur town headquarters. Offers boating, picnic spots, and panoramic valley views from an inspection bungalow on an adjacent hill.
facts: Favourite local tourist spot at outskirts of district HQ
Small but scenic lake with surrounding foliage
Inspection bungalow available for overnight stays

name: Sendra Island
description: Hillock island in Loktak Lake rising from the water, linked by a walkway, offering panoramic views of floating phumdis and the lake. Popular tourist park with bungalow and cafeteria for sunset views.
facts: About 50 km from Imphal
Part of Loktak tourist circuit with Keibul Lamjao
Ideal for photography of phumdis

name: Moirang Town
description: Historic town in Bishnupur district, sacred in Manipuri culture as origin of Khamba-Thoibi epic. Gateway to Loktak Lake and site of INA flag hoisting; about 45 km from Imphal.
facts: Origin of Khamba-Thoibi love epic
INA headquarters in 1944
Elevation ~766 m

name: Sadu Chiru Waterfall
description: Picturesque multi-tier waterfall (also known as Leimaram) near the Bishnupur-Senapati border, about 20 km from Imphal beside Tiddim Road. Cascades in lush forested hills with clear pools.
facts: Listed on Bishnupur district official tourism site
Three-tier falls; accessible via short walk
Flag: near Senapati district border (Sadar Hills area)

name: Shree Shree Govindajee Temple
description: Historic Vaishnavite temple with twin golden domes in the Palace Compound, Imphal East district. Built in 1846 by Maharaja Nara Singh (rebuilt 1876), it is the largest Vaishnava temple in Manipur and a major pilgrimage site adjoining the former royal palace.
facts: Presiding deity Radha Govinda; flanked by Krishna-Balaram and Jagannath group
Part of Spiritual Circuit under Swadesh Darshan Scheme
Daily aarti and festivals like Janmashtami and Rath Yatra
About 1-2 km from city center; confirmed Imphal East by official and Wikipedia

name: Andro Village and Mutua Bahadur Museum
description: Traditional Loi/Chakpa village about 21-26 km east of Imphal in Imphal East, known for black pottery and cultural heritage. Home to Mutua Bahadur Museum / Andro Cultural Complex with tribal house replicas, artifacts, pottery, manuscripts and orchids.
facts: Scheduled Caste village developed as cultural hub
Museum founded by Mutua Bahadur; exhibits from NE tribes
Famous for traditional pottery and sacred fire at Panam Ningthou
About 25 km from Imphal on Imphal-Yairipok road

name: Santhei Natural Park
description: Eco-tourism park at the fringe of Andro village in Imphal East, featuring an artificial lake/dam, green hills, walking trails and picnic spots. Developed through community efforts and NEC funding for nature conservation.
facts: About 21-24 km from Imphal
Popular local picnic and nature spot
Infrastructure developed with NEC support 2013-14
Adjacent to cultural sites in Andro

name: Kaina Temple / Sacred Jackfruit Tree
description: Sacred hillock about 29 km east of Imphal on Imphal-Yairipok road in Imphal East (border area). Site where King Bhagyachandra is said to have received divine guidance to carve the Govindajee idol from a jackfruit tree; features temple and pilgrimage importance.
facts: Linked to legend of Shree Govindajee idol carving
Tourist homes managed by Manipur Tourism
Elevation around 900+ m
Flag: some older sources list near Thoubal; official Imphal East lists it

name: Sanamahi Kiyong Temple (Nongmaiching)
description: Temple dedicated to Lainingthou Sanamahi, ancient Meitei deity, on the summit of Nongmaiching (Selloi Langmai) hills in Imphal East. Center for Sanamahism followers; completed 2019 in classical Meitei architecture with views over the valley.
facts: Elevation ~980 m on Nongmaiching hill (peak ~1565 m)
Pilgrimage for Meitei, Kabui, Zeliangrong communities
Associated with University of Sanamahi Culture project
About 15-20 km from Imphal

name: Sekta Archaeological Living Museum
description: Open-air living archaeological museum at Sekta village, Imphal East, on the banks of the Iril River. Protected site with excavated burial mounds revealing secondary burial practices of medieval Proto-Meitei communities; excavated by ASI and state archaeology.
facts: About 16 km northeast of Imphal on Imphal-Ukhrul road
One of six mounds; 0.35 acre protected area
Excavated 1991-94; evidence of 14th-15th century practices
Also known as Sekta Kei

name: Marjing Polo Complex and Statue
description: Sports and cultural complex on Heingang Ching (Marjing Hill) in Heingang, Imphal East. Houses the world's tallest equestrian statue of a polo player (122 ft / 37 m), dedicated to God Marjing, the Meitei deity of polo (Sagol Kangjei) and horses. Celebrates Manipur as the cradle of modern polo.
facts: About 9 km from Imphal
Statue inaugurated 2023 by Union Home Minister
23-acre complex with horse grazing grounds
Sacred site for Marjing worship and polo traditions

name: Hanuman Thakur Temple (Mahabali)
description: Historic temple dedicated to Lord Hanuman on the banks of the Imphal River in Mahabali forest, Wangkhei area of Imphal East. Built in 1725 by King Garib Niwaj in Bengal hut-style brick architecture; only temple from that reign, with a stone idol in human form.
facts: Built 1725 AD; evidence of Ramanandi cult in Manipur
Surrounded by Mahabali forest with resident monkeys that stay within bounds
About 3-5 km from city center in Wangkhei
Listed on official Imphal East tourism site

name: Tipaimukh
description: Historic confluence of the Barak (Tuiruong) and Tuivai rivers at the southern tip of the Vangaitang range in Pherzawl district, marking a traditional trade route and the proposed site for the Tipaimukh Dam.
facts: Mouth of the Tuivai River joining the Barak River
Historic Khongjai route trade point to Assam and beyond
Forms part of the Manipur-Mizoram boundary
Proposed embankment dam site for flood control and hydroelectric power
Elevation around 50-63 m

name: Senvawn Village
description: Historic Hmar village in Pherzawl district known as the birthplace of Christianity in southern Manipur, where Welsh missionary Watkin Roberts arrived in 1910, transforming local communities.
facts: Also known as Senvon or Kawnzâr
Established by early Hmar settlers; cradle of education in the region
Located on Senvon Range near the Tuivai River
Population around 3,136 (2011)
About 22 km from Tipaimukh

name: Pherzawl Town
description: District headquarters of Pherzawl, a hill town established in 1894 amid lush forests and rivers, serving as the administrative and cultural center for the Hmar-dominated region.
facts: Headquarters of Pherzawl district formed in 2016 from Churachandpur
Elevation around 1,037 m
Founded by Bulhmang Infimate in 1894
Connected via NH-2 and local roads; helicopter service nearby at Parbung
Literacy rate high at ~85.75% (2011)

name: Parbung
description: Hmar village and headquarters of Tipaimukh Sub-Division in Pherzawl district, featuring a community health centre, heliport under construction, and access via National Highway 2.
facts: Also known as Bungkhawpui
Founded in 1897 by Ngamneivung
Primary healthcare hub for the district
NH-2 connects to Mizoram
Population around 2,545 (2011)

name: Taithu Village
description: Remote Hmar village in the Vangai Range of Pherzawl district, known for traditional lifestyles, terraced fields, ginger cultivation, and scenic hillside trails.
facts: Founded in 1920; originally called Rengpui Bung
NH-2 passes through the village
Population around 1,173 (2011)
Specializes in ginger farming
Offers authentic tribal cultural experiences

name: Lungthulien
description: Hmar village near which stand the Lungthu Lien Pathum (Three Large Trivets), massive ancestral stones erected around 1852, part of the Hmar ethnic cultural landscape.
facts: Home to ancient stone trivets linked to Hmar settlement history
Population around 1,714 (2011)
Part of broader Hmar Ethnic Cultural Sites including Sikpui Lung
Remote access requires local guidance
Reflects pre-Christian animistic traditions

name: Phulpui Village
description: Isolated Hmar village near the Barak River associated with the tragic love legend of Zawlpala and Talvungi, featuring historical graves and a prayer cave.
facts: Famous for Mizo-Hmar Romeo and Juliet-style legend
Near Barak River with cliff-edge views
Home to Pastor Thangngur's Prayer Cave
Population around 750 (2011)
Preserved traditional hill culture

name: Barak River (Pherzawl Section)
description: Major river flowing through Pherzawl district, known locally as Tuiruong, forming scenic valleys, gorges, and the Tipaimukh confluence with the Tuivai.
facts: Also called Tuiruong in local languages
Forms part of Manipur-Mizoram boundary in places
Vital for local communities and transport historically
Supports proposed Tipaimukh Dam project
Scenic sections ideal for nature walks and photography

name: Tuivai River
description: River flowing through southern Pherzawl hills that joins the Barak at Tipaimukh, offering clear waters and forested banks in an offbeat landscape.
facts: Also known as Tipai River
Confluence at Tipaimukh is a key landmark
Borders sections with Mizoram
Supports local ecology and potential for rafting/angling
Flows through dense forests of the district

name: Lainingthou Sanamahi Kiyong (Sanamahi Kiyong)
description: Temple of the Meitei deity Lainingthou Sanamahi on Nongmaiching (Selloi Langmai) hills in Imphal East. Centre for Sanamahism followers; completed around 2019 in traditional Meitei architectural style at about 980 m elevation. Pilgrimage site for Meitei, Kabui and Zeliangrong communities.
facts: On Nongmaiching hills, Imphal East
Dedicated to Lainingthou Sanamahi of Sanamahism
Elevation around 980 m; Meitei architecture
Consecrated/completed 2019
Official tourist and pilgrimage place

name: Kaina Temple / Sacred Hillock
description: Sacred hillock about 29 km east of Imphal on the Imphal–Yairipok road in Imphal East (Keirao area). Site associated with the legend of King Bhagya Chandra receiving guidance to carve a Govinda idol from a sacred jackfruit tree; features a temple complex and is a Hindu pilgrimage spot.
facts: About 29 km east of Imphal on Yairipok road
Sacred jackfruit tree legend linked to King Bhagya Chandra
Hindu pilgrimage site with temple complex
Elevation around 900+ m
Official tourist place; tourist home nearby

name: Khuga Dam (Tuitha Dam / Mata Dam)
description: Multipurpose dam on the Khuga (Tuitha) River south of Churachandpur town, inaugurated in 2010. Popular picnic and viewpoint spot with reservoir, hills and greenery; height 38 m, length about 230 m. Local attraction for nature and photography despite incomplete hydro power functions.
facts: South of Churachandpur (Lamka) town on Khuga River
Construction started 1983, resumed 2002, inaugurated 2010 by Sonia Gandhi
38 m high and ~230 m long
Popular local picnic and scenic spot
Official tourist place of Churachandpur district

name: Ngaloi Waterfall (Ngaloimoul Falls)
description: Cascading waterfall near Ngaloi (Ngaloimoul) village, about 9 km from Churachandpur town. Set against low hills and dense greenery with foamy white water over dark rocks; one of the most accessible and popular nature spots in the district.
facts: About 9 km from Churachandpur town
Near Ngaloi / Ngaloimoul village on Tipaimukh Road
Multi-tier cascade in green foothills
Popular short day-trip and photography spot
Official tourist place listed by Churachandpur NIC

name: Tonglon Caves
description: Historic caves in Singngat sub-division of Churachandpur district, noted for carvings, sculptures and engravings linked to early tribal settlements. Archaeological and cultural site offering insight into regional history amid forested hills; requires short trek.
facts: In Singngat sub-division, Churachandpur district
Known for ancient carvings and scripts
About 10–32 km from Churachandpur depending on route
Archaeological link to early settlements
Official tourist place of the district

name: Tuibuong Tribal Museum
description: Ethnographic museum on Tedim Road in Tuibuong area of Churachandpur showcasing tribal artefacts, costumes, tools, weapons and household items of Zo, Kuki, Paite, Hmar and other hill communities. Educational hub for tribal heritage of southern Manipur.
facts: On Tedim Road in Tuibuong / near Lamka town
Displays costumes, tools, weapons and crafts of local tribes
About 2 km from main Churachandpur centre
Focus on Zo/Kuki-Chin-Mizo cultural heritage
Listed among official places of interest

name: Churachandpur Town (Lamka)
description: Second-largest town in Manipur and headquarters of Churachandpur district, locally known as Lamka. Bustling tribal hub on Tiddim/Tedim Road about 60 km south of Imphal, known for Kuki-Chin-Mizo markets, handicrafts and as gateway to southern hills and nature spots.
facts: About 60 km south of Imphal on Tiddim Road
Local name Lamka (road junction); preferred by residents
District HQ and major commercial centre for hill tribes
Known for indigenous handicrafts and tribal markets
Base for visits to Khuga Dam, Ngaloi and Tonglon

name: Lunjang Waterfall
description: Remote cascading waterfall in the hills near Pamzal / Lunjang village area, about 20–25 km from Churachandpur town. Requires a short trek through forest; quieter offbeat alternative to Ngaloi with natural pools and dense greenery.
facts: About 20–25 km from Churachandpur town
Near Pamzal / Lunjang village; last section by trek
Less crowded than Ngaloi Falls
Surrounded by forested hills
Emerging local nature and picnic spot

name: Suangdoh Village
description: Historic tribal village in the southern part of Churachandpur district along Guite Road, inhabited mainly by Paite community. Offers cultural immersion with traditional stilt houses, jhum cultivation views, church architecture and nearby treks in hilly terrain.
facts: In Singngat / southern Churachandpur area
Primarily Paite community settlement
Headquarters of Suangdoh sub-division
Traditional houses and cultural practices
Gateway for rural and nature experiences

name: Pamzal Reserved Forest
description: Forested reserve area near Pamzal in Churachandpur district offering wildlife and nature experiences amid hills. Supports local biodiversity and serves as backdrop for nearby waterfalls and village tourism; suitable for short nature walks and birdwatching.
facts: Near Pamzal area in Churachandpur district
Reserved forest supporting local flora and fauna
Proximity to Lunjang and other falls
Suitable for nature and birdwatching
Part of southern Manipur hill ecosystems

name: Tamenglong Town
description: District headquarters of Tamenglong, a hill town at about 1,400–1,580 m elevation in the Naga hills of western Manipur, known as the Land of the Hornbill and Exotic Orchids. Base for exploring Barak waterfalls, Zeilad lakes, Tharon Cave and Rongmei/Liangmai/Zeme cultural sites.
facts: HQ of Tamenglong district
Elevation around 1,389–1,580 m
About 150–160 km from Imphal
Land of the Hornbill
Orange Festival held in December

name: Barak Waterfalls
description: Series of seven waterfalls along the Barak River in Tamenglong, a scenic rafting and picnic spot amid dense forest. Popular for its turquoise pools, rock formations and relative remoteness; one of the district’s signature attractions.
facts: Series of seven falls on Barak River
Near Zeilad area
Rafting and picnics popular
About 15–20 km from Tamenglong HQ
Best October–February

name: Tharon Cave
description: Ancient limestone cave system (also Kalemki or Thaeuluan) about 27 km from Tamenglong HQ near Tharon village. Approximately 655 m long with five exits and 34 joints; archaeological finds link to Hoabinhian culture; map engraved at entrance; home to fruit bats.
facts: ~655 m long with 5 exits
About 27 km from Tamenglong HQ
Hoabinhian archaeological links
Map engraved at entrance
Locally known as Kalemki (house of bats)

name: Zeilad Lake
description: Largest of a cluster of sacred natural lakes (Zeilad, Guiphop Zei, Nrou Zei, Nap-sam Zei and others) near Makoi/Atengba, part of Zeilad Wildlife Sanctuary. Known for pythons, fish, tortoises and waterbirds; scenic hilltop setting with local folklore ties to Rani Gaidinliu.
facts: Part of Zeilad Wildlife Sanctuary (est. 1997)
Cluster of several lakes
About 15–20 km from Tamenglong
Home to pythons and waterbirds
Associated with Naga folklore

name: Buning Meadow
description: Expansive rolling meadow (also Npiulong) near Tamei sub-division, about 15 km from Tamenglong HQ. Characterized by small mounds, brooks, ground orchids and wild lilies in early summer; popular for birdwatching and nature walks.
facts: Near Tamei sub-division
About 15 km from Tamenglong HQ
Ground orchids and wild lilies in summer
Home to birds and small wildlife
Also called Npiulong

name: Kisha Khou
description: Magnificent cliff and mountain viewpoint near Tamenglong used for trekking. Historically associated with Rani Gaidinliu as a hideout during the 1930s–40s freedom movement; scenic and culturally significant.
facts: Cliff for trekking near Tamenglong
Hideout of Rani Gaidinliu 1935–40
Official tourist place listed by district
Scenic views
About 12 km from HQ

name: Khoupum Dam
description: Earth-fill dam in Khoupum Valley, Nungba sub-division, constructed in the late 1970s and noted as one of the early such structures in Northeast India. Scenic valley setting with surrounding hills and local villages.
facts: First earth-fill dam in Northeast India (late 1970s)
In Khoupum Valley, Nungba sub-division
About 100 km from Tamenglong HQ
Scenic reservoir and hills
Local landmark

name: Zeiladzang Village
description: Serene Zeliangrong tribal village in Tousem sub-division, primary base for exploring the Zeilad group of lakes. Offers cultural immersion, traditional houses and access to surrounding natural attractions.
facts: In Tousem sub-division
Base for Zeilad lakes
Zeliangrong community
Natural beauty and culture
Official tourist listing

name: Dailong Village
description: Village known for biodiversity, birdwatching (including hornbills) and nearby Nroutamphang/Dailong Waterfall. Offbeat spot for nature enthusiasts and cultural experience among local Naga communities.
facts: About 10 km from Tamenglong
Dailong/Nroutamphang Waterfall nearby
Hornbill and bird habitat
Community and nature focus
Listed on official district gallery

name: Kangla Fort
description: Historic fortified palace complex in central Imphal that served as the traditional seat of the Meitei kings of the Ningthouja dynasty until 1891. Features temples, moats, museums, and cultural relics on the western bank of the Imphal River.
facts: Traditional seat of Meitei rulers until British annexation in 1891
Located in Imphal West district at the heart of the capital
Includes Pakhangba Temple and Kangla Sha dragon statues
Official tourist place listed by Imphal West NIC
Open to public with free entry

name: Ima Keithel (Women's Market)
description: Asia's largest all-women market in central Imphal at Khwairamband Bazar, run exclusively by thousands of Meitei women vendors selling produce, textiles, fish, and handicrafts. A unique cultural and economic landmark reflecting women's traditional role in commerce.
facts: Established in the 16th century; one of the largest women-run markets in Asia
Over 3000-5000 women vendors operate the stalls
Located west of Kangla Fort in Imphal West
Official tourist place listed by Imphal West NIC
Split into sections for produce and handlooms

name: Shaheed Minar
description: Tall memorial monument in Bir Tikendrajit Park commemorating Meitei and tribal martyrs of the 1891 Anglo-Manipur War, including Yubaraj Bir Tikendrajit and General Thangal who were hanged nearby.
facts: Erected in memory of martyrs from the 1891 Anglo-Manipur War
Located in Bir Tikendrajit Park near Polo Ground in Imphal West
Features three vertical beams with mythical dragons at the top
Official tourist place listed by Imphal West NIC
About 1-2 km from Kangla Fort

name: Nupi Lal Memorial Complex
description: Memorial complex in central Imphal honoring the courageous Manipuri women who led the Nupi Lal (Women's War) uprisings against British colonial policies in 1904 and 1939, particularly the rice export protests.
facts: Commemorates the 1939 Nupi Lal women's uprising against British rice exports
Located near Imphal Head Post Office in Imphal West
Features statues and records of the women's resistance
Official tourist place listed by Imphal West NIC
Observed annually on 12 December as Nupi Lal Day

name: Manipur State Museum
description: State museum near the Polo Ground and Kangla Fort displaying Manipur's tribal heritage, ethnology, archaeology, natural history, and portraits of former rulers, including a large royal boat exhibit.
facts: Inaugurated in 1969 by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi
Located near Imphal Polo Ground in Imphal West
Galleries on ethnology, archaeology, and natural history
Official tourist place listed by Imphal West NIC
Houses the 78-ft Hiyang Hiren royal boat

name: Manipur Zoological Garden
description: Zoo at Iroisemba in Imphal West, about 6 km west of Imphal city at the foot of pine-covered hillocks on the Imphal-Kangchup road. Home to the endangered Sangai (brow-antlered deer) and other endemic species.
facts: Established in 1976; second habitat of the Sangai deer after Keibul Lamjao
Located in Iroisemba, Imphal West district
Recognized by Central Zoo Authority for Sangai conservation breeding
Official tourist place listed by Imphal West NIC
About 6 km west of Imphal city center

name: Imphal War Cemetery
description: Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery in Imphal West commemorating over 1,600 Allied soldiers who died in the 1944 Battle of Imphal during World War II. Maintained as a peaceful memorial site.
facts: Contains approximately 1,600 Commonwealth burials from WWII
Located in Kabo Leikai, Imphal West on the Imphal-Dimapur road
Maintained by the Commonwealth War Graves Commission
Commemorates soldiers from the Battle of Imphal 1944
Confirmed in Imphal West district

name: Khonghampat Orchidarium
description: Botanical garden and orchid conservation center maintained by the Manipur Forest Department near Khonghampat village, about 7-12 km north of Imphal on NH-2. Houses hundreds of orchid species including rare endemic varieties.
facts: Established in 1976 by Manipur Forest Department
Spreads over about 200 acres near Khonghampat, Imphal West
Houses over 110-500 orchid species including rare ones
Peak blooming season April to July
Located about 7-12 km from Imphal on Imphal-Dimapur highway

name: Imphal Town
description: Capital city of Manipur and headquarters of Imphal West district, serving as the nodal center of the oval-shaped Imphal Valley at about 790 m elevation. Gateway to the state's major tourist circuits including Loktak and hill districts.
facts: State capital and district HQ of Imphal West
Located at the center of the Imphal Valley
Elevation approximately 786-790 m
Major transport hub with international airport
Base for exploring Kangla, Ima Keithel, and surrounding attractions

name: Kakching Garden (Uyok Ching)
description: Hilltop ecological park and tourist centre at Uyok Ching south of Kakching town, featuring manicured gardens, rose garden, unique topiary plants (including green elephant), panoramic valley views, and religious sites including Ibudhou Pakhangba Temple and Mahadev Temple.
facts: Developed as major tourist centre attracting local and foreign visitors
Houses traditional Meitei architecture Pakhangba shrine and Shiva temple
About 45 km from Imphal Airport; 2 km from Kakching bus stand
Site of cultural programmes and community gatherings

name: Kakching Town
description: District headquarters and major commercial hub in southeastern Manipur, known as the 'Rice Bowl of Manipur' and declared the cleanest city in Northeast India in 2018. Important trading centre for vegetables, fish and rice.
facts: Formed as separate district in 2016 from Thoubal
Elevation around 776 m
About 44-45 km southeast of Imphal
Famous for Kakching Haraoba festival and local dialect

name: Sugnu Town
description: Southern trading centre and town on the bank of the Imphal/Manipur River, offering scenic river views. Partly in Kakching district (municipal area) with adjacent areas in Chandel.
facts: About 74 km from Imphal on Imphal-Sugnu State Highway
Important commercial point in southern district
Bridge over Manipur River for east-west connectivity
Flag: Municipal portion in Kakching; some villages in Chandel

name: Pallel Town
description: Border town and gateway between the plains of Kakching and hill areas of Chandel, on the Indo-Myanmar road (NH-102/Asian Highway). Known for multi-ethnic market with hill products and handicrafts.
facts: About 46 km southeast of Imphal on NH-39/102
Meeting place of plain and hill communities
Elevation around 830 m
Daily market with agricultural products and handicrafts

name: Kakching Aerodrome
description: World War II era aerodrome used by British forces, now largely non-functional and associated with military use. Historic airstrip remains visible.
facts: Strategic WWII airfield during Imphal campaign
Coordinates approximate from historical mapping
Near Kakching town; currently restricted or military-related

name: People's Museum Kakching
description: Private rural ethnographic and historical museum founded in 1981 by Mayanglambam Gourachandra, housing rare manuscripts (puyas), prehistoric tools, tribal ornaments, traditional costumes, pottery, musical instruments and artifacts from Meitei and other communities of Manipur.
facts: First rural museum of Manipur, established 1981
Collection includes nearly 1200 rare manuscripts and Stone Age artefacts
Located in Paji Leikai, Kakching
Entry fee applies; open daily with seasonal timings

name: Kakching Irabot Memorial Park
description: Memorial park in Kakching town dedicated to Hijam Irabot Singh, freedom fighter and cultural figure, offering a peaceful space with cultural monuments.
facts: Honours contributions of Hijam Irabot
Located near central Kakching on Sugnu-Imphal road area
Popular for local visits and relaxation

name: Kharungpat Bird Sanctuary
description: Recently notified wildlife sanctuary covering about 227 hectares of the Kharungpat wetland in southern Kakching district, third-largest freshwater lake area after Loktak and Pumlen. Important habitat for resident and migratory waterbirds.
facts: Notified under Wildlife Protection Act 1972 as state's eighth wildlife sanctuary
2023 census recorded 69 bird species, ~40% migratory
About 35 km south of Imphal; planned for eco-tourism development
Coordinates approximate; exact boundary TBD

name: Pumlen Pat
description: Second-largest freshwater lake in Manipur after Loktak Lake, located in Kakching district. Features floating phumdis, supports local fisheries and communities; faces challenges from siltation and encroachment. Forms part of a larger wetland system with Khoidum Pat and Lamjao Pat.
facts: Approximately 68 km south of Imphal and 45 km from Thoubal
Wikipedia coordinates: 24°25′N 93°52′E (24.42, 93.87)
Important wetland proposed in past for Sangai deer translocation
Primarily in Kakching district post-2016 reorganization (flag: some older sources list under Thoubal)

name: Tengnoupal Town
description: Hill town and district headquarters of Tengnoupal, located at the highest point on NH-2 between Imphal and Moreh. Offers bird's-eye views of surrounding hills and the Kabaw Valley plains in Myanmar. Elevation about 1450 m; foggy during monsoon, cool summer winds.
facts: Created as district HQ after 2016 split from Chandel
Name derived from cactus fencing (teng = cactus, pal = fence)
Strategic location on ASEAN Highway / India-Myanmar corridor
Sources: Wikipedia Tengnoupal, OSM

name: Moreh Town
description: International border town on the India-Myanmar border in Tengnoupal district, gateway to Kabaw Valley. Major trade hub with Integrated Check Post (ICP), known for cross-border commerce and cultural exchange.
facts: Established around 1829; key India-Myanmar trade point
AH1 and Trans-Asian Railway connectivity plans
Population about 16,800 (2011)
Sources: Wikipedia Moreh, OSM

name: Yangoupokpi-Lokchao Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Indo-Burma wildlife sanctuary near the India-Myanmar border, covering about 185 sq km. Represents unique biodiversity of the two zones; home to Hoolock gibbon, bears, serow, leopard, and occasional elephants. Best visited October to April.
facts: Established 1989; IUCN category IV
Only ape in India (Hoolock gibbon) found here
Rest houses at Moreh; older sources list under Chandel (pre-2016 split)
Sources: Wikipedia, OSM, local reports

name: Machi
description: Village and subdivision headquarters in Tengnoupal district, part of the administrative structure along the Imphal-Moreh corridor.
facts: One of the three sub-divisions: Tengnoupal, Moreh, Machi
Sources: Official district info, OSM

name: Kwatha Village
description: Village near Yangoupokpi-Lokchao Wildlife Sanctuary in Tengnoupal district, offering access to the sanctuary's biodiversity and border landscapes.
facts: Located in Tengnoupal subdivision
Proximity to Indo-Myanmar border forests
Sources: OSM

name: Lokchao River
description: River flowing through Tengnoupal district near the wildlife sanctuary and border areas, contributing to the region's ecological diversity.
facts: Associated with Yangoupokpi-Lokchao WLS
Sources: OSM

name: Hindu Temple Moreh
description: Hindu place of worship located in Moreh town, serving the local community in the border area.
facts: Listed in OpenStreetMap as place of worship
Sources: OSM

name: Kamjong Town
description: District headquarters of Kamjong, a hill town about 120 km from Imphal on the Ukhrul-Kamjong road, serving as gateway to eastern Manipur hills and Indo-Myanmar border areas. Predominantly Tangkhul Naga and Thadou communities.
facts: Created as district HQ in 2016 after bifurcation from Ukhrul
Elevation around 1500-1560 m
About 120 km from Imphal; nearest airport Imphal
Gateway to remote border villages and waterfalls

name: Khayang (Tililytiluelue) Waterfall
description: Scenic waterfall in the forest of Khayang Village, Kamjong district. Officially listed as a natural/scenic beauty site; reported as one of the tallest in Manipur in local accounts, popular for trekking and adventure.
facts: Located about 60 km from Kamjong HQ in Khayang Village forest
Also known as Tililytiluelue
Requires local guide; access via rough roads
Part of official district tourist places list

name: Liabi Waterfall
description: Waterfall located in the forest of Chatric / Siyang Village, Kamjong district. Multi-tiered cascade in dense subtropical forest, accessible via trek from the border village.
facts: Also called Chatric Waterfall; near Chatric/Siyang Village
About 40 km from Kamjong HQ, partially on Ukhrul-Kamjong highway
Border village setting with views toward Myanmar/Chindwin
Official tourist place; best with local guide

name: Kazeiram (Land of the Dead)
description: Mythological site significant to Tangkhul Naga belief, regarded as the place of the spirit world or land of the dead. Features non-man-made stone steps (Kazei Keirak) believed to lead to it, located at Hangou Kaphung.
facts: Official tourist place; about 85 km from Kamjong HQ
Kazei Keirak stone steps considered the ladder to the spirit world
Important in Tangkhul oral traditions and folklore
Remote access; cultural significance over commercial tourism

name: Kazei Kharalung
description: Site famous for natural sharpening stones available in the region, listed among official tourist places of Kamjong district.
facts: About 72 km from Kamjong HQ
Known for quality sharpening stones
Official district tourist place
Remote location in Tangkhul area

name: Chatric (Siyang) Village
description: Traditional Tangkhul Naga border village (also called Siyang) southeast of Kamjong, on the Indo-Myanmar border near Chindwin River. Known for Liabi Waterfall, freshwater fish, King Chilli (Sivathei), and views of Myanmar hills.
facts: About 40 km from Kamjong HQ; Indian border village with Myanmar
Home to Chatric tui dialect speakers; all Christian
Famous for Liabi Waterfall and local King Chilli festival
Views of Mt. Chawki and Chindwin valley

name: Kongkan Village
description: Remote Tangkhul Naga settlement on the Indo-Myanmar border ridge in Kamjong district, offering panoramic views into Myanmar. Traditional houses with wood carvings; gateway-like position near border pillars.
facts: Approximately 15-45 km from Kamjong depending on route; near border
Traditional Naga architecture and terrace farming
Strategic border location with Myanmar views
Limited access; community guest arrangements possible

name: Phungyar Town
description: Small town and subdivision headquarters south of Kamjong in Kamjong district. Home to Kamo Tangkhul community, administrative and educational hub for surrounding villages, on routes connecting Imphal area to eastern hills.
facts: Subdivision HQ; about 50 km from Ukhrul, south of Kamjong
Population ~953 (2011); Kamo Tangkhul dialect
Vidhan Sabha constituency of the same name
Market and educational center for remote villages
